Connect to foundations: The virial theorem: why shrinking stars heat up ↗ Compare solution assumptions and boundary data in the solution library ↗ 01Smooth gravity and discrete encounters A star orbits in a cluster’s mean field and is weakly deflected by individual neighbours. Relaxation measures accumulated velocity changes becoming comparable to the original velocity. It is distinct from direct physical collisions. Two-body refers to an encounter approximation, not a two-star model of the cluster. Assume equal masses, roughly isotropic velocities and many weak deflections. 02One deflection and its encounter rate For a nearly straight passage with relative speed v and sufficiently large impact parameter b, integrate the transverse gravitational acceleration over the encounter. Δv⊥≈2Gmbv, dΓ=2πb n v db n is stellar number density. Add squared, randomly directed kicks. The larger number of distant encounters compensates their smaller individual deflections, giving comparable contributions per logarithmic impact interval. d⟨Δv²⟩dt≈8πG²m²nv∫bminbmaxdbb=8πG²m²nvlnΛ Λ≡bmaxbmin, trel≈v³8πG²m²n lnΛ 03Coulomb logarithms and cluster scaling The analogous encounter integral gives the name Coulomb logarithm, although the force here is gravity. Estimate bmin near the large-angle scale Gm/v² and bmax near the system size; the integral has physical cutoffs. v²∼GNmR, tcross∼Rv, trel∼NlnΛtcross Combining the preceding impulse model with a uniform virial sphere gives a coefficient of 1/6. Distribution-averaged coefficients differ; do not mix this estimate with a precision convention. 04Compare half-mass relaxation times Adopt the following conventional equal-mass half-mass relaxation estimate. The coefficient 0.138 and choice ln(0.4N) are supplied conventions, not exact consequences of the uniform-sphere calculation. tdyn≡√(rh³GNm), trh≈0.138Nln(0.4N)tdyn The panel fixes m = 0.5 solar masses, so total mass grows with N. Dynamical time scales as N⁻¹ᐟ² and relaxation approximately as N¹ᐟ²/lnN. Always state which quantities are held fixed. 05Toward segregation and distribution evolution A mass spectrum introduces systematic energy exchange and a tendency for heavier objects to segregate inward. Complete equipartition need not follow. Binaries, strong encounters, tides and stellar evolution also affect long-term evolution. Collecting small mean changes and variances into continuous coefficients leads to the Fokker–Planck equation. This panel recomputes timescale estimates, not an N-body trajectory of a particular cluster. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. Raise N from 10⁴ to 10⁵ at fixed stellar mass and half-mass radius. How do dynamical and half-mass relaxation times change? Show the answer and reasoning Dynamical time decreases by √10. Relaxation time changes by √10 ln(4000)/ln(40000) ≈ 2.48. The panel fixes mass per star; fixing total mass instead gives the ratio of N/ln(0.4N).
